en: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to me: Anas—meaning Ibn 'Iyad Abu Damrah—narrated to me, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "While three persons were walking, rain overtook them, so they took shelter in a cave in a mountain. Then a rock fell from the mountain over the mouth of their cave, shutting them in. Some of them said to others: 'Look to righteous deeds you performed for Allah and supplicate Allah, Exalted is He, by them, so that perhaps Allah will relieve you from it.' One of them said: 'O Allah, I had two aged parents, a wife, and young children for whom I used to shepherd [flocks]. When I brought them back to rest in the evening, I milked [the herd] and began with my parents, giving them milk to drink before my children. One day the search for pasture took me far away, so I did not return until evening and found them both asleep. I milked as I used to milk and brought the milking vessel, standing by their heads; I disliked waking them from their sleep, and I disliked giving milk to the children before them, while the children were crying at my feet. That remained my condition and theirs until dawn broke. If You know that I did that seeking Your Countenance, then open for us an opening through which we may see the sky.' So Allah opened an opening for them through which they saw the sky. Another said: 'O Allah, I had a female cousin whom I loved as passionately as men love women. I sought her intimate favors, but she refused unless I brought her one hundred dinars. I toiled until I gathered one hundred dinars and brought them to her. When I sat between her legs, she said: "O servant of Allah, fear Allah, and do not break the seal except lawfully." So I stood up from her. If You know that I did that seeking Your Countenance, then open for us an opening.' So He opened [it further] for them. And the other said: 'O Allah, I had hired a laborer for a faraq of rice. When he finished his work, he said: "Give me my due." I offered him his faraq, but he turned away from it. I kept cultivating it until I amassed from it cattle and their herdsmen. Then he came to me and said: "Fear Allah, and do not wrong me of my due." I said: "Go to those cattle and their herdsmen and take them." He said: "Fear Allah and do not mock me." I said: "I am not mocking you; take those cattle and their herdsmen." So he took them and went away with them. If You know that I did that seeking Your Countenance, then open for us what remains.' So Allah opened what remained."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Maslamah, who said: I heard Aba Nadrah narrating from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, the world is sweet and green, and indeed Allah has appointed you as successors in it to see how you will act. So beware of the world and beware of women, for the first tribulation of the Children of Israel was in women." And in the hadith of Ibn Bashshar: "so that He may see how you will act."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr both narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us; all of them from Sulayman al-Taymi, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, Suwayd ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la all narrated to us from al-Mu'tamir; Ibn Mu'adh said: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: My father said: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Harithah and Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, that they both narrated from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "I have not left behind me among the people any tribulation more harmful to men than women."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Sufyan and Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I have not left behind me any tribulation that is more harmful to men than women."

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abd al-Karim Abu Zur'ah narrated to us: Ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: Among the supplications of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your blessing, the transformation of Your [grant of] well-being, the suddenness of Your retribution, and all of Your wrath."

And Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Mutarrif narrating that he had two wives, with the meaning of the hadith of Mu'adh.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah had two wives. He came from the presence of one of them, so the other asked: "Have you come from the presence of so-and-so?" He replied: "I have come from the presence of 'Imran ibn Husayn, and he narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, the fewness among the dwellers of Paradise are women.'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah: He heard Aba Raja' from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... and he mentioned the like of it.

And Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) looked into the Fire... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Ayyub.
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Al-Thaqafi informed us: Ayyub informed us with this chain of transmission.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas saying: Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I looked into Paradise and saw the majority of its dwellers to be the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw the majority of its dwellers to be women."

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us; all of them from Sulayman al-Taymi; (H) and Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn—and the wording is his—narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I stood at the gate of Paradise, and lo, the majority of those who entered it were the destitute, while the people of wealth and status were held back, except the people of the Fire, for they had been commanded to the Fire. And I stood at the gate of the Fire, and lo, the majority of those who entered it were women."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mu'awiyah—and he is Ibn Salih—informed me, from Rabi'ah ibn Yazid, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "The servant will continue to have his supplication answered so long as he does not supplicate for sin or severing ties of kinship, as long as he is not hasty." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is hastiness?" He said: "He says: 'I have supplicated and I have supplicated, but I did not see that He answers me,' so at that point he gives up hope and abandons supplication."

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn Layth narrated to me: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that he said: Abu 'Ubayd, the freed slave of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf—and he was among the reciters and people of legal understanding—narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One of you will be answered so long as he is not hasty, saying: 'I have supplicated to my Lord, but He has not answered me.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu 'Ubayd, the freed slave of Ibn Azhar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One of you will be answered so long as he is not hasty, saying: 'I have supplicated, but it has not'—or—'so it has not been answered for me.'"
And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr—and the wording is Ibn Numayr's—both narrated to us: Abu Usamah and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah is well pleased with the servant when he eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Safwan—and he is Ibn 'Abdullah ibn Safwan—and al-Darda' was married to him; he said: I arrived in the Levant (al-Sham) and came to Abu al-Darda' at his dwelling, but I did not find him, and I found Umm al-Darda'. She said: "Do you intend to perform Hajj this year?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Then supplicate to Allah for good for us, for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: 'The supplication of a Muslim person for his brother in his absence is answered; at his head is an appointed angel, and whenever he supplicates for his brother for good, the angel appointed over him says: "Amin, and for you the like."'" He said: Then I went out to the marketplace and met Abu al-Darda', and he said the like of that to me, relating it from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he said: from Safwan ibn 'Abdullah ibn Safwan.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: Musa ibn Sarwan al-Mu'allim narrated to us: Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Kariz narrated to me, saying: Umm al-Darda' narrated to me, saying: My master (Abu al-Darda') narrated to me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel appointed over him says: 'Amin, and for you the like.'"

Ahmad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs al-Waki'i narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Kariz, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No Muslim servant supplicates for his brother in his absence except that the angel says: 'And for you the like.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Jurayri, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Jasri, from 'Anazah, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Shall I not inform you of the most beloved words to Allah?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of the most beloved words to Allah." He said: "Indeed, the most beloved of words to Allah is: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise)."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Habban ibn Hilal narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Sa'id al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Jisri, from Ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked: "Which words are best?" He said: "What Allah chose for His angels or for His servants: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise)."

And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that whenever an affair distressed him, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would say... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Mu'adh from his father, and added along with them: "There is no god but Allah, Lord of the noble Throne."

And 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrated to them from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to supplicate with them and say them at times of distress... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham from his father, from Qatadah, except that he said: "Lord of the heavens and the earth."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham with this chain of transmission; and the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham is more complete.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ibn Bashshar, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id—and the wording is Ibn Sa'id's—narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say at times of distress: "There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the magnificent Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the noble Throne."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Layth narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah of His bounty, for they have seen an angel; and when you hear the braying of a donkey, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for it has seen a devil."

Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Ayshi narrated to me: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: Rawh—and he is Ibn al-Qasim—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that Fatimah came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking him for a servant and complaining of the work, so he said: "You will not find that with us." He said: "Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than a servant? You glorify Allah (say Subhan Allah) thirty-three times, praise Allah (say Al-hamdulillah) thirty-three times, and magnify Allah (say Allahu Akbar) thirty-four times when you take your place of rest." And Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated it to me: Habban narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us with this chain of transmission.
